items.title: Headlines for November 19, 2026 | Democracy Now!
items.excerpt: ## Trump Blasts ICC, Praises Presidents Xi and Putin at Unprecedented Trilateral Summit Nov 19, 2026 The leaders of Russia, China and the United States — Presidents Vladimir Putin, Xi Jinping and Donald Trump — have wrapped up an unprecedented trilateral summit in Shenzhen, China, with what Chinese media is calling a landmark “peace declaration.” The four-point plan calls for the three nations to reduce nuclear risks, increase oil refining, promote reforms to the United Nations and limit the jurisdiction of the International Criminal Court. This is President Trump. > President Donald Trump: “In another area of potential cooperation between us, I’ll be suggesting ways to protect our nation’s sovereignty from rogue globalist organizations such as the International Criminal Court, which has gotten out of control, which I believe we all agree has really strayed far from beyond its jurisdiction.” President Putin faces an ICC warrant seeking his arrest for war crimes committed in Ukraine, including the unlawful transfer of children from Russian-occupied areas. Neither the U.S., nor China, nor Russia is a party to the Rome Statute that established the International Criminal Court. During the summit, President Trump lavished praise on President Xi and referred to President Putin as “my friend.” That prompted Polish Prime Minister Donald Tusk to write on social media, “God, protect us from such friends.” ## Democrats Nominate Hakeem Jeffries for Speaker as Progressives Dissent on Healthcare, Gaza and ICE Nov 19, 2026 On Capitol Hill, House Democrats voted 251-11 on Wednesday to nominate New York Congressmember Hakeem Jeffries to be the next speaker of the House. Jeffries is poised to make history as the first African American to fill the role. The vote came during a closed-door caucus meeting. Afterward, seven incoming Democratic congressmembers issued a joint statement explaining their opposition to Jeffries. They wrote, “Whether on Medicare for All, stopping ICE terror, getting money out of politics, or ending the genocide in Gaza, our constituents sent us to Congress with a mandate on these issues.” ## Israeli Tanks and Bulldozers Push Past Gaza’s “Yellow Line,” Further Displacing Palestinians Nov 19, 2026 In Gaza, thousands of Palestinians have been forced to flee again after Israeli tanks and bulldozers pushed past the ceasefire’s “Yellow Line” on Wednesday and into Palestinian-held territory. Israeli troops operating east of the “Yellow Line” have gradually pushed the boundary westward and now occupy about two-thirds of Gaza’s territory, with 2 million Palestinians trapped in an increasingly narrow strip of land, most of them forced to live in tents. This is Salam Aql, a Palestinian woman who says she was displaced for the 15th time on Wednesday. ... Israeli Defense Minister Israel Katz said the military is ready to take more land and turn the newly seized areas into permanent parts of Israel’s security zones. The Palestinian Health Ministry says Israeli forces have killed over 1,600 Palestinians in Gaza since last October’s so-called ceasefire. ... ## World Court Finds Burma Committed Genocide Against Rohingya in 2017 Nov 19, 2026 Judges at the International Court of Justice have found that Burmese security forces committed genocide against Rohingya Muslims during military operations nearly a decade ago. It’s the first time the court has held a nation accountable for violating the 1948 Genocide Convention. The ruling follows the 2017 military crackdown by government forces and ethnic Rakhine mobs that killed about 10,000 people and drove more than 730,000 Rohingya into Bangladesh. Ahead of today’s verdict, survivors hoped the ICJ would deliver justice and pave the way for them to return to their homeland. ... ## Venezuela Restores Military Ties with U.S., Months After Abduction of President Maduro Nov 19, 2026 Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth made a surprise visit to Caracas on Wednesday, where he announced the U.S. and Venezuela have signed an agreement to restore military ties. Under the deal, the two countries will work together on areas such as joint training, intelligence sharing and border security. It’s Hegseth’s first visit to Venezuela since U.S. forces violently abducted former President Nicolás Maduro and his wife, National Assembly deputy Cilia Flores, back in January. The deal comes after months in which Washington has effectively controlled Venezuela’s oil sales. ... ## Anthropic Valued at $1.5 Trillion Ahead of Initial Public Offering Anthropic has become the first major AI lab to become a publicly traded corporation, after completing what’s become the largest initial public offering in history. On Wednesday, Anthropic said it had raised a record $107.3 billion, giving it a valuation of more than $1.5 trillion. This comes after Anthropic warned in its IPO filings that, without proper safeguards, its technology poses “catastrophic or existential risks to humanity.”

items.title: Higher fuel prices seep into core inflation - Dallasfed.org
items.excerpt: November 19, 2026 Fuel prices have been on a wild ride since late February 2026, when military strikes on Iran set off sharp moves in oil and fuel markets. Retail gasoline prices aside, the U.S. retail diesel price reached an all-time high, the jet fuel price is near its previous peak, and the heating oil price has set a new record. The U.S. price of natural gas, meanwhile, has barely budged. The fuel price surge has been very uneven. Diesel prices in particular moved sharply higher. Diesel is the fuel of the freight economy. Trucks, trains, ships and farm equipment run on it, which means its price may potentially touch the cost of moving nearly everything consumers buy. The price gap between diesel and gasoline has widened significantly in recent months. On Sept. 22, 2026, the national average retail price of diesel reached $6.53 per gallon, about 70 percent above its level at the end of February (compared with a 50 percent rise for retail gasoline). The diesel rise surpassed the fuel’s previous record set in 2022 (Chart 1). Prices have eased only modestly, to about $6.31 as of the end of October. Consumers experience these prices directly at the pump and indirectly on their utility bills. But fuel prices may also work their way into the prices of other goods and services, from airline tickets to paper towels. Economists call these "second-round effects," and they matter for the Federal Reserve because they show up in core inflation, an inflation measure that excludes food and energy. Policymakers watch core inflation closely to gauge underlying price pressures. Our estimates suggest that higher fuel prices added between 20 and 60 basis points to 12-month core inflation, as measured by the personal consumption expenditures (PCE) price index, as of September 2026. If fuel prices simply held at their current levels, that contribution would gradually decline by about 30 basis points by the end of 2027. ... By construction, core PCE inflation excludes energy. But excluding energy prices from the index doesn't insulate it from their effects. When fuel costs rise, airlines tend to charge more for tickets, shippers tend to raise freight rates and manufacturers that rely on energy-intensive inputs seek to pass along higher costs. The size of these second-round effects is not clear a priori because not all producers can pass on fuel price increases. For ... All of our estimates point to the same conclusion: The pass-through of fuel prices to core PCE inflation is generally small and difficult to estimate precisely, but because this year's fuel price swings have been so large, their second-round effects on core inflation are not negligible.

items.title: Up First briefing: Hakeem Jeffries; Trump meets Xi, Putin; Anthropic : NPR
items.excerpt: House Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries has received the House Democrats' nomination to become speaker when the party regains the majority in the new year. This nomination, confirmed by a closed-door vote of 251 to 11, marks the start of the formal selection process for speaker. It will culminate in a House floor vote on Jan. 3, at the start of the new Congress. If successful, Jeffries will make history as the first Black Speaker of the House. Jeffries said after the closed door vote that he is committed to addressing cost-of-living issues, pledging to fight for lower costs in groceries, gas, housing and healthcare. ... - 🎧 Jeffries, who has served as the top Democrat in the minority since 2023, ran unopposed for the speaker position. But that is not the case in the Senate, NPR's Elena Moore tells Up First. Current minority leader Sen. Chuck Schumer faces a challenge from Sen. Chris Van Hollen for majority leader. Van Hollen has positioned himself as an anti-status quo, progressive leader. Both Van Hollen and Schumer have served in Congress for decades. The vote for that Senate position is set for early December. - ➡️ Rep. Robert Garcia, poised to chair the House Oversight Committee, sent document-preservation letters to more than a dozen of President Trump's allies and family members in preparation for investigations starting in January. These letters focus on four main areas: "Trump family corruption, corporate corruption, DHS misconduct and the White House Epstein cover-up."

items.excerpt: Actor Robert Downey Jr. revealed that he initially wondered whether there were any surprises left for him in the Avengers franchise after his character Iron Man's emotional exit in "Avengers: Endgame". Marvel Studios released a featurette featuring the Oscar winner, who discussed his decision to return to the Marvel Cinematic Universe franchise, this time playing its antagonist Victor Von Doom, also known as Doctor Doom, in the upcoming film "Avengers: Doomsday". ... ## Saif Ali Khan Receives Death Threat Bollywood actor Saif Ali Khan has reportedly received a death threat from someone claiming to be Zeeshan Akhtar, who is wanted in connection with the 2024 murder of politician Baba Siddique. The police are now trying to establish whether Akhtar was actually involved in sending the threat or if someone else used his name to target celebrities and create trouble for law enforcement agencies. This is not the first such incident reported this month. Actors Tusshar Kapoor and Ayushmann Khurrana had also received similar threats earlier. Police arrested 30-year-old Vaibhav Mishra, an IIT graduate from Bengaluru, in connection with both cases. Investigators found no links between Mishra and any criminal gang. He allegedly used artificial intelligence (AI) to send the threatening messages. ... ## Ramayana Box Office Collection Day 14 Ramayana has surpassed Aditya Dhar's Dhurandhar at the Indian box office within just two weeks of its release. According to Sacnilk, the film earned Rs. 23.20 crore net in India on Day 14, taking its total domestic net collection to Rs. 844.40 crore. Its India gross collection has now reached Rs. 1,009.05 crore. With this, Ramayana has moved ahead of Dhurandhar, which had collected Rs. 840.20 crore net in India after its release in December last year. The achievement comes just 14 days into Ramayana's theatrical run. However, the film's overseas performance appears to be slowing down. It added Rs. 8 crore gross from international markets on Day 14, taking its overseas gross collection to Rs. 510 crore. Meanwhile, its worldwide gross collection has reached Rs. 1,519.05 crore. ... Speaking to TIME magazine as part of its TIME100 Next India feature, Alia Bhatt addressed the online discussions about her marriage to Ranbir Kapoor and the claims that she is in an ‘unequal marriage’. The actress called such assumptions offensive, saying people were reducing her to someone who would silently suffer in an imaginary situation. Alia also suggested that the speculation could stem from the fact that her relationship does not follow conventional ideas of marriage. Explaining what makes her bond with Ranbir special, she said, "The bedrock of any relationship is when you feel seen without putting any effort, and feel heard without saying anything—that’s Ranbir for me, and that’s our reality."
